concepts.name: Real Gases & van der Waals Equation
concepts.summary: Real gas equation: $\left(P + \frac{a n^2}{V^2}\right)(V - nb) = nRT$. Constant $a$ measures magnitude of intermolecular attractive forces; constant $b$ measures effective molecular volume (co-volume $b = 4 V_m$). Compressibility factor $Z = \frac{PV}{nRT}$: for ideal gas $Z=1$; at low pressure $Z < 1$ (attraction dominates); at high pressure $Z > 1$ (repulsion dominates). Real gases approach ideal behavior at HIGH temperature and LOW pressure.
concepts.common_traps: For Hydrogen and Helium, attractive forces are negligible ($a \approx 0$), so $Z = 1 + \frac{Pb}{RT} > 1$ at all ordinary temperatures!
concepts.tips_and_tricks: A gas with higher critical temperature $T_c$ and higher $a$ value is more easily liquefied (e.g. $\text{NH}_3, \text{SO}_2$ liquefy more easily than $\text{N}_2, \text{H}_2$).

concepts.name: Ideal Gas Laws, Dalton's Law & Graham's Diffusion
concepts.summary: Ideal gas equation: $PV = nRT = \frac{w}{M}RT \implies P M = d R T$. Dalton's law: $P_{\text{total}} = \sum P_i$, where $P_A = \chi_A P_{\text{total}}$. Graham's law: rate of diffusion $r \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}$.
concepts.common_traps: Graham's law uses the inverse square root of molar mass: lighter gas diffuses faster ($\text{H}_2$ diffuses 4 times faster than $\text{O}_2$ because $\sqrt{32/2} = 4$).
concepts.tips_and_tricks: Gas density formula $d = \frac{PM}{RT}$. At higher temperature and lower pressure, gas density is minimum.

## 2. Comprehensive Concept Deep-Dive & Source PYQ Links

### 2.1 Real Gases & van der Waals Equation (Real Gases)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **7 PYQs** (Moderate Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Real gas equation: $\left(P + \frac{a n^2}{V^2}\right)(V - nb) = nRT$. Constant $a$ measures magnitude of intermolecular attractive forces; constant $b$ measures effective molecular volume (co-volume $b = 4 V_m$). Compressibility factor $Z = \frac{PV}{nRT}$: for ideal gas $Z=1$; at low pressure $Z < 1$ (attraction dominates); at high pressure $Z > 1$ (repulsion dominates). Real gases approach ideal behavior at HIGH temperature and LOW pressure.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\left(P + \frac{a}{V_m^2}\right)(V_m - b) = RT, \quad Z = \frac{V_{\text{real}}}{V_{\text{ideal}}}, \quad T_c = \frac{8a}{27Rb}
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: For Hydrogen and Helium, attractive forces are negligible ($a \approx 0$), so $Z = 1 + \frac{Pb}{RT} > 1$ at all ordinary temperatures!

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: A gas with higher critical temperature $T_c$ and higher $a$ value is more easily liquefied (e.g. $\text{NH}_3, \text{SO}_2$ liquefy more easily than $\text{N}_2, \text{H}_2$).

#### Linked Representative PYQs:
- **[2024 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"Identify the wrong relation for real gases :..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2022 Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"Which property of $CO_{2}$ makes it biologically and geo-chemically important?..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2022 Shift] Q#3 (MCQ)**: *"The volume of $2.8g$ of $CO$ at $27^{\circ}C$ and 0.821 atm pressure is
( $R=0.08210\text{L. atm K}mol^{-1}$ )..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2021 Shift] Q#4 (MCQ)**: *"When the absolute temperature of ideal gas is doubled and pressure is halved, the volume of gas..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

### 2.2 Ideal Gas Laws, Dalton's Law & Graham's Diffusion (Gas Laws)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **1 PYQs** (Standard Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Ideal gas equation: $PV = nRT = \frac{w}{M}RT \implies P M = d R T$. Dalton's law: $P_{\text{total}} = \sum P_i$, where $P_A = \chi_A P_{\text{total}}$. Graham's law: rate of diffusion $r \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}$.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
PV = nRT, \quad P = \frac{dRT}{M}, \quad \frac{r_1}{r_2} = \sqrt{\frac{M_2}{M_1}} = \frac{V_1 / t_1}{V_2 / t_2}
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Graham's law uses the inverse square root of molar mass: lighter gas diffuses faster ($	ext{H}_2$ diffuses 4 times faster than $	ext{O}_2$ because $\sqrt{32/2} = 4$).

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Gas density formula $d = \frac{PM}{RT}$. At higher temperature and lower pressure, gas density is minimum.

#### Linked Representative PYQs:
- **[2019 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"Which of the following equations does not represent Charles's law for a given mass of gas at constant pressure?..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring KCET Pitfalls in States of Matter

### 1. Speed & 80-Second Constraint Management
KCET demands answering 60 questions in 80 minutes (~1.33 minutes per question). The most lethal trap is spending 3+ minutes on long algebraic derivations. Always check for dimensional consistency or option substitution first.

### 2. NCERT & Karnataka PU Board Direct Lines
Over 45% of KCET theory questions are taken directly from NCERT / Karnataka PU Board textbook summary points, margins, and standard exemplar questions. Pay rigorous attention to exceptions (e.g., electron gain enthalpy of Cl vs F, acidic nature of boric acid, non-polar symmetrical geometries).

### 3. Unit Conversions & Prefix Overlooks
Units of molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), micro/nano multipliers (10^-6, 10^-9), and centimeter-to-meter conversions in optics and gravitation account for the highest frequency of careless mark losses in KCET.

### 4. No Negative Marking Advantage
Since KCET has NO negative marking, never leave any question unattempted. When down to two options, use dimensional elimination or parity checks to maximize expected score.
